subject: Pilot credits — structuring, tax treatment, and invoicing path
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@launchpad.inc>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot credits - tax and invoicing Qs

Hi Tessa / Laura,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Before we formalize the pilot SOW, our finance team flagged a few questions about the $25k promotional credit package you proposed for the Launchpad cohort:

- How will the credits show up on our invoices? Do you send a $0 invoice, an invoice with line-item credits, or simply no invoice until we consume billable overages?
- From a tax standpoint, does Redwood treat promotional credits as taxable consideration in the US? Our tax lead asked whether we should be recognizing them as marketing expense or as contra-revenue on our books.
- If there are overages beyond credits, how will those be invoiced and when will they be due?

Can you loop in whoever owns revenue recognition/legal so we can confirm on our side? Also attaching a short list of our finance contacts.

Appreciate the help — hoping to get this locked before our onboarding on Oct 4.

Best,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Partnerships | Launchpad Inc.
attachments: Launchpad_finance_contacts.csv (csv)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@launchpad.inc>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot credits - tax and invoicing Qs

Samir — thanks for the clear list. Quick replies inline, then next steps below.

1) Invoice surface: our standard for cohort promos is to issue a formal invoice that lists the subscription/usage lines and a separate credit line (negative amount) so your accounting system retains an invoice record. We can also provide a $0 invoice if you prefer a single document that shows net zero.

2) Tax treatment: Redwood's default is to treat promotional credits as a contra-revenue/marketing allowance for our revenue team, but the tax treatment can vary by jurisdiction and customer accounting policy. I'll loop in Legal/RevRec to create a short memo for Launchpad.

3) Overages: overage usage is invoiced monthly in arrears and is due net 30 from invoice date. We can set a billing threshold carveout for this pilot (e.g., no automatic charge under $500 without pre-approval).

Next steps (proposed):
- I'll attach a draft SOW that reflects the credit amount and the invoicing presentation (attached).
- Ben, could you run the draft by Finance to confirm the invoice template?
- Laura / Mina, can Legal/RevRec produce a 1-page memo on tax/accounting treatment for Launchpad?

If that's agreeable, Samir, we'll send a formal SOW + accounting memo by Friday.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Startup Partnerships | Redwood Inference
attachments: pilot-sow-draft.docx (docx), Launchpad_Tax_Qs.pdf (pdf)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot credits - tax and invoicing Qs

Tessa / Ben — quick internal note before we send anything external.

- Accounting: we generally record promotional credits as a contra-revenue line and defer recognition over the pilot term where appropriate. For a $25k one-off credit tied to an onboarding pilot (<= 90 days), we usually book a contra-revenue and apply it against recognized revenue when usage occurs.
- Tax: Mina, can you confirm whether US sales/use tax or other indirect taxes apply to promo credits? My sense is credits reduce taxable transaction amount but not always — depends on taxable event definitions.
- Invoicing form: Ben, please confirm we can produce an invoice with a clearly labeled "Promotional Credit" line and an accompanying credit memo if Launchpad prefers separate docs.

I'll wait on Mina's note and then Tessa can send the memo + SOW.

-Laura

Laura Bennett
Partner Operations Lead | Redwood Inference
